correctness.rationale: For n>=3, every one of 2n side triangles contains at least one frustrated edge. Each rim frustration has one triangle incidence and each cross-edge frustration two; hence 2d+r_a+r_b>=2n and F>=n+(r_a+r_b)/2. Rim parity forces r_a,r_b even/odd with n. Equality gives alternation on both even rims (4 states) or precisely one defect on each odd rim (2 n^2 states). The explicit forced bottom-spin construction proves all odd defect pairs valid and accounts for the exact M=0,+/-2 counts. Finite-volume fluctuation-response gives the stated Curie coefficient; two genuinely separate graph enumerators check n=3..9 and squared-cycle dynamic programming checks n=3..80. Analytic proof covers all n, finite tests do not substitute for it.

value.rationale: An n-gonal antiprism is a canonical triangular ladder, so the finite size, sign of coupling and parity of its cyclic closure are natural features, not arbitrarily chosen parameters. The result completely classifies its ground-state manifold and magnetization distribution for all n>=3; the even/odd switch between 4 and \(2n^2\) states has a measurable zero-temperature finite-size Curie-response distinction. It is a structural frustrated-lattice benchmark with independent proof and explicit physical interpretation, not a numeric finite-size census or a renamed textbook inequality. No thermodynamic singularity is claimed.
